title: Thailand Provincial HIE Feed Operations
thesis: A fictional provincial health information exchange in Thailand receives FHIR bundles from 40 facilities in Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Khon Kaen, Hat Yai and Phuket. Snowflake turns that facility-level feed activity into completeness and data quality KPIs, 7-day interface incident risk, unmapped code anomalies and cited AI answers, with no patient data.

talking_points: Start with the exchange as a whole: feed completeness, accepted bundles, rejection rate and interface incidents for 40 facilities in 5 Thai cities.
Each card is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table; run_core.py recomputes them from RAW on every build.
The issue-type chart separates the data quality issues that become interface incidents from those closed without escalation, such as the two city-wide network outages.
tabs.call_out: One set of exchange KPIs that traces back to facility-day rows

transition.line: Which facilities should the interface team call first this week?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification gives each facility a probability of an interface incident in the next 7 days. It is an integration operations score, not a clinical prediction.
The holdout line reports precision and recall on the most recent labelled days against the base rate, so the team knows how far to trust the ranking.
Anomaly detection flags unusual unmapped code rates per facility, and the forecast projects accepted bundles for the next 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Evaluated ML that runs where the feed data lives

transition.line: Are conformance checks keeping pace with the feeds?

talking_points: Conformance check compliance, FHIR profile conformance and pending profile reviews show where onboarding work is still open.
The scatter plots check compliance against interface incidents per facility; it shows an association in synthetic data, not a cause.
The action memo drafts three interface actions for the week from the KPI, facility, issue-type and risk tables only, for a person to review.
tabs.call_out: A grounded draft, with a person deciding

transition.line: What happens when a slow bundle batch arrives right now?

talking_points: New bundle delivery events land in RAW.LIVE_BUNDLES, from the Snowflake simulator or from S3 PutObject through Snowpipe. They carry facility-level metrics only.
The alert logs each ALERT event with a playbook hint and the facility risk band, then emails the exchange integration team.
tabs.call_out: From a late batch to a follow-up in one platform

transition.line: Now ask the exchange data directly.

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers metric questions through Cortex Analyst over the semantic view, and procedure questions through Cortex Search over 14 synthetic interface playbooks.
Every answer shows the generated SQL and the playbook IDs it cited.
tabs.call_out: Answers the integration team can check

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: One core, two builds: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake with S3, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q.
The exchange, facilities and people are fictional and the data is synthetic; a fresh clone rebuilds the same figures.
tabs.call_out: One governed core with an optional AWS layer
